title: Watermark-based capacity signalling and tenant-tier backoff playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a hosted API outage on 2026-02-10 we observed rapid GPU capacity exhaustion in the us-west-2 default pool leading to queue amplification, high tail latency, and customer-facing 503s. This ticket captures the novel root-cause findings and codifies a staged mitigation + long-term prevention playbook built around watermark-based capacity signalling and tenant-tier backoff policies.

Root cause: A confluence of three factors: (1) Autoscaler cooldown was overly conservative after a previous flapping event (cooldown 6m) which delayed provisioning when multiple medium-sized tenants burst concurrently; (2) a subtle change in our logging service upstream induced a short-lived retry storm from a subset of customers, amplifying request fanout into the queue; (3) no soft-preemption or tenant-degrade policy was in place, so queues built evenly across tenants leading to head-of-line blocking and slow KV-cache warming on newly scheduled replicas.

Why this is different from prior incidents: instead of single-tenant hotloops or total underprovisioning, this incident was a multi-tenant cadence problem where small bursts across many tenants combined with autoscaler hysteresis created a non-linear queue growth. Previous playbooks focused on prewarm and immediate scale; this requires coordinated admission control plus smarter signalling so we avoid repeated over-scale/under-scale cycles.
action_items: Short-term (P0): Implement emergency runbook entries for manual watermark escalation: on detection of 90% GPU util + 3x baseline enqueue rate, oncall can trigger immediate prewarm of a spare pool. Owner: Marco Liu. Due: 2026-02-18.

Short-term (P0): Deploy a temporary tenant-concurrency throttle for lowest-priority tenants (tier: free/experimental) to cap concurrent in-flight requests at 2 until stabilization. Owner: SRE team (rotation). Due: 2026-02-14.

Medium-term (P1): Ship watermark signalling: add low-watermark (40%), high-watermark (75%), and emergency-watermark (92%) sensors per GPU pool that emit a signed capacity signal to the admission controller. Admission controller will progressively reduce allowed concurrency per-tenant at each watermark. Owner: Infra runtime team. Estimate: 5 points. Due: 2026-03-10.

Medium-term (P1): Implement tenant-tier decay counters and burst tokens: enterprise tenants retain larger token buckets; free tiers have faster decay/penalty to discourage retry storms. Owner: Platform team. Estimate: 5 points. Due: 2026-03-20.

Medium-term (P1): Autoscaler tuning: reduce cooldown from 6m -> 90s when emergency-watermark observed and enable opportunistic prewarm policy that uses historical burst profiles for top 50 tenants. Owner: Autoscaling SIG. Estimate: 3 points. Due: 2026-03-15.

Long-term (P2): Synthetic tenant-stress simulator to reproduce multi-tenant pulse patterns and validate watermark thresholds and backoff policies in staging. Owner: Reliability Eng. Estimate: 8 points. Due: 2026-04-30.

Long-term (P2): KV-cache warmstart improvements: prioritize cache-warm on newly scheduled replicas for tenants that contributed >10% of enqueues in previous 5m window. Owner: Serving runtime team. Estimate: 8 points. Due: 2026-05-15.
Follow-up: Update documentation and runbooks: add explicit detection heuristics, escalation steps, and post-incident checklist for runbook authors. Owner: Oncall docs lead. Due: 2026-03-01.
postmortem_summary: Impact: ~27 minutes of elevated tail latency and rate-limited 503s for 6% of production requests in us-west-2; several mid-market customers reported timeouts. Detection: Spike in enqueue rate alerted by token bucket anomaly detector at 02:13 UTC; escalation occurred at 02:18 UTC. Mitigation: manual prewarm + tenant throttle at 02:20 UTC reduced queue length and restored baseline by 02:40 UTC. Root causes enumerated above. Action plan includes immediate throttles, watermark signalling, and autoscaler changes.
comments: 2026-02-10 02:22 - Marco Liu: Manually prewarmed two G4 pools and applied tiered throttle; observed queue drain starting at ~02:28. Confirmed free-tier accounts were responsible for 46% of the excess enqueues (token-bucket logs attached).

2026-02-15 16:03 - Priya Sharma (SRE): Deployed short-term free-tier throttle (feature flag toggled) and validated across two regional pools during a synthetic 10m storm; throttles held queues below high-watermark in test. Metrics: 88% reduction in queue growth rate under the same synthetic load.

2026-02-25 11:12 - Ben Gomez (Autoscale): Proposed autoscaler change: introduce emergency cooldown override that bypasses normal hysteresis for 15m after emergency-watermark. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscale/pull/421

2026-03-08 14:02 - Marco Liu: Implemented prototype of watermark signal (prometheus rule + Redis pubsub) in staging; admission controller reads from Redis channel and applies per-tenant backoffs. Observed expected behavior in 3/3 staging runs. Next: harden auth and signal integrity.
